missionPara1: To ensure healthy and safe work environment, and enable professional development and career enhancement for healthcare worker.
heroHeadline: Built by healthcare workers, for healthcare workers.

history.text: Public Sector Pay Framework — A Major Win — MHPU’s advocacy contributed to the extension of the Pay Framework to local workers across the public sector, including healthcare support staff and other public service workers.
MHPU registered as a trade federation under the Industrial Relations Act

Overtime Campaign — A Major Win — Following MHPU’s campaign, the Public Sector Pay Framework Standards were amended to ensure work on public holidays is paid as overtime without counting toward the overtime cap.
Overtime Campaign Escalation — Escalated the overtime campaign to daily online picketing, intensifying calls for fair compensation for healthcare workers working beyond the prescribed overtime limit.

Maternity Policy Reform Campaign — Launched a campaign to reform the existing maternity policy by addressing gaps in provisions for fostering and adoption, fertility and related medical treatments, pregnancy and infant loss, workplace childcare facilities, and other family-friendly workplace measures.

Occupational Safety & Health Advocacy Campaign — Launched a workplace-focused campaign to promote safer and healthier working environments and strengthen awareness of occupational safety and health rights.

Launch of “Heyriyaa” — Launched MHPU’s union advocacy television programme Heyriyaa in collaboration with NTV, providing a platform to advocate for workers’ rights and discuss wider issues affecting workers, their families, and society, including social justice, public accountability, occupational safety, healthcare, resource management, and good governance.

Industrial Relations & OSH Acts — Legislative Milestone — The Industrial Relations and Occupational Safety & Health Bills were ratified by the President, becoming Acts and strengthening the legal framework for workers’ rights and workplace safety.

IR & OSH Bills — A Collective Advocacy Win — Following sustained advocacy by MHPU and other Maldivian unions since 2019, Parliament passed the Industrial Relations and Occupational Safety & Health Bills, strengthening the legal framework for workers’ rights and workplace safety.

A worker with an undergraduate degree holds an equivalent position— A Major Win — Following MHPU’s pressure  the President’s Office directed the Civil Service Commission to place undergraduate degree holders in their designated positions(PS7) under the new Pay Framework, benefiting qualified civil servants across the public service, including healthcare workers.

Healthcare Job Structure Campaign — Secured the implementation of job structures for technical healthcare workers, marking a major milestone in MHPU’s campaign, while advocacy for support staff continued.

Overtime Campaign — Launched a campaign against the 10% overtime cap introduced under the new Pay Framework, advocating for fair compensation for healthcare workers required to work beyond the cap due to staffing shortages.

Thaareeheh Hoadhan & Support Staff Matter Campaigns — Launched weekly online picketing campaigns to intensify the job structure campaign and advocate for the inclusion of healthcare support staff in the new job structures.
MHPU affiliated with Public Services International (PSI), the global union federation representing workers in public services.
Black Ribbon Campaign — Launched a nationwide campaign advocating for the establishment of structured job classifications and a fair State Pay Framework for healthcare workers.
Founded by a small group of laboratory technologists with a vision to unite healthcare workers and advance their rights, welfare, and professional interests.

heroLede: Maldives Health Professionals Union is the labour federation representing and advocating for the rights, welfare, and professional interests of both local and expatriate healthcare workers, including professional and support cadres, working across the Maldives.
guides: Independence — Maintaining independent union decision-making, free from employer or political influence.
Solidarity — Standing together to protect the rights, dignity, and welfare of all healthcare workers, with every member treated equally regardless of role, profession, nationality, or island.
Accountability — Ensuring union leadership is elected by the members and remains transparent, responsible, and accountable to them.
ctaText: Members can stand for regional representative roles, join a bargaining committee, or help organise in their workplace.
